threads.body: [General] This guard drops `otel.event.name` structured arguments whenever no attribute selector is configured (including the default and deprecated `false` cases). Previously, structured arguments were still processed with a null attribute predicate, and `captureLogstashMarker` extracted `otel.event.name` before applying that predicate; the README also documents event-name support independently of attribute capture. Keep processing structured arguments with a null predicate so attributes remain disabled while event names continue to work.

replies.body:
You're right, and this was a real regression — `main` has no predicate guard here, and `captureLogstashMarker` extracts `otel.event.name` before consulting the (nullable) predicate, so my guard silently disabled event names from structured arguments in the default and deprecated-`false` cases. It was also inconsistent with the Logstash marker path a few lines above, which passes the nullable predicate straight through.

Removed the guard and left a comment explaining why the arguments are processed unconditionally. Added `eventNameIsCapturedWithoutSelector` to `LogstashStructuredArgsSelectorTest`, and confirmed it actually catches this: with the guard reinstated it fails, and passes once removed.
